summary: A pair of range lights at the mouth of the Red River in Lake Winnipeg, lit in 1895; the 1913-14 front tower now stands at the Marine Museum of Manitoba in Selkirk.

light.characteristic: fixed white (the 1895 back light, per the 1895 description); the successor Red River Mouth light is Fl W 4s, seasonal

structures.note: Built 1913 or 1914 (sources differ). About 27 ft (8.2 m); dioptric lens (LighthouseFriends). Moved to the Marine Museum of Manitoba grounds in Selkirk in 1992 (LighthouseFriends; Selkirk Museum). Standing.
Two-section steel skeletal tower with an enclosed wooden top; catoptric apparatus (LighthouseFriends). Demolished in 1992 (LighthouseFriends; Selkirk Museum).
Modern range towers placed at the entrance in 1992; in service until 2019. The rear tower was renamed the Red River Mouth light in 2019.

access.note: Grounds of the Marine Museum of Manitoba in Selkirk open; tower closed (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).

visit.note: Front tower stands on the Marine Museum of Manitoba grounds; tower closed.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (range lights and successor light); Marine Museum of Manitoba (front tower)

events.note: Lightship placed at the mouth of the Red River, built by John and Charles Short for $2,468; fixed white light 21 ft above the water.
Lightship beached at the western mouth and used as a shore light until 1893; the lantern moved to a pole in the eastern channel.
Pair of range lights at the mouth of the eastern channel, in operation 2 September 1895.
New range towers; LighthouseFriends dates the work to 1913 (M.J. Egan oversaw, $3,091). Selkirk Museum and Rowlett give 1914.
Front tower of the 1913-14 set moved to the Marine Museum of Manitoba grounds in Selkirk.
Rear tower of the 1913-14 set demolished.
Modern range towers placed at the entrance to the Red River.
Front range light discontinued; rear light renamed the Red River Mouth Light (still active, seasonal, per CCG list).

keepers.name: Hughie Reed

corrections.why: The 1992 date is when the 1913-14 towers were replaced. The modern range towers placed in 1992 served until 2019 (LighthouseFriends; Selkirk Museum). Rowlett's 'inactive since 1992' describes the old front tower on display in Selkirk.

The current point is the Selkirk museum, where the 1913-14 front tower stands. The range lights stood at the river mouth on Lake Winnipeg. Proposed: the position of the successor Red River Mouth (Main Channel) light, 50 23 22.9 N, 096 48 29.2 W (CCG list). Approximate: the sources give no coordinates for the 1895 or 1913-14 sites.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends dates the new towers to 1913; the Selkirk Museum and Rowlett give 1914. The Museum says the buildings 'were replaced in 1914'; LighthouseFriends says 'In 1913, new range lights were built'. Both are cited; the story gives both.
Rowlett's 1895 (station established) and LighthouseFriends' 1880 lightship are both right: the lightship was the first light at the mouth; the range lights date from 1895.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on the 1913 vs 1914 rebuild and on Hughes's start (1883 in LighthouseFriends and the Museum, 1885 in one LighthouseFriends passage, appointment 12 Feb 1892 in the Department keepers' lists). The keepers' lists are OCR tables in which names, dates and salaries sit in separate blocks: Hughes's 1892 date was matched by position beside 'Red River Range' in the FY1911 list (scan 256) and the FY1914 list (scan 77), and the FY1909 list (scan 178) prints 'Red Rock. Red River Range (see Snug Harbour)' with the same date. The checker should read those page images. The 1895 description is quoted as LighthouseFriends prints it; the 1895 report itself is not in the local corpus (corpus starts 1900). The Winnipeg Tribune items (1914 new lights photo caption, 17 Aug 1925 interview) are known only through LighthouseFriends and the Museum; none was read directly. Chronicling America search for the station returned nothing relevant; Canadian newspapers are not in that archive. Distances in the 1895 description are in feet and miles as printed (miles are not nautical miles). The record's coordinates point at the Selkirk museum, not the river mouth (see corrections). The record's 'status: inactive' is correct for the range; the successor light is active (seasonal). Keeper Hughie Reed has no dates in any source. Keeper Spence's family detail comes from an unnamed newspaper article as relayed by LighthouseFriends; treat as secondhand. Verified 2026-10-28 by the fact-checker: the FY1911 keepers' list (scan 256) and the FY1914 list (scan 77) were read as page images; the Red River Range row (William Hughes, Feb. 12, 1892, under 'Appointed') is printed in both, and the 1914 row sits in its own position in the station column. The FY1911 table also prints Wm. Hughes, Feb. 12, 1892 against Black Bear Island (400.00), and the FY1914 table gives Black Bear Island to D. Matheson (June 22, 1899); the story now states this. The 1912 report's February 1912 inspection (scan 41) was read in the OCR and matches. Corrections from the page checks: the 'square' new front tower is supported by the Selkirk Museum, not LighthouseFriends alone.
